transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [name]. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Um, well, I came in because I've been having some trouble with my eating lately. After my late shifts at work, I'll usually stop for food, but then I just... keep going once I get home. Like, I'll eat a full takeout meal, and then I'll start on chips, sweets, really whatever's in the apartment. And afterward, I'm just shocked by how much I actually ate. It's, uh, it's starting to really bother me.
After one of these episodes where you feel you've eaten a large amount, do you ever do anything to try to compensate for it—like make yourself vomit, use laxatives, fast, or exercise excessively?

Yeah. Um, sometimes after I get home and eat too much of that takeout or all those snacks, I'll go to the bathroom and make myself throw up. I just... I do it so the food won't just sit in me and turn into weight. So, yeah, that's what I've been doing.
How often would you say these episodes of overeating followed by making yourself throw up happen, and how long has this pattern been going on?

Um, well, I guess it really started since my apartment move settled into a routine. Since then, I'd say most weeks I have at least one late-night episode where I just eat way past what I meant to. And then... I try to make up for it. Usually by throwing up, like I mentioned, or sometimes I'll just skip breakfast the next day, or force myself to go on a really long run to burn it off.
How many months has this weekly pattern of overeating and then purging or compensating been going on?
Um, I'd say it's been about a year and five months now. It started right after I moved into this temporary apartment near the tourist district for my job. So, yeah, since then.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports recurrent episodes of binge eating (consuming large amounts of food with a subjective sense of loss of control, feeling 'shocked' by the amount eaten) occurring at least weekly for over a year. These episodes are followed by compensatory behaviors including self-induced vomiting, fasting (skipping breakfast), and excessive exercise (long runs) aimed at preventing weight gain. The frequency (≥1x/week) and duration (>3 months, actually ~17 months) exceed the DSM/ICD threshold for Bulimia Nervosa. No indication of significantly low body weight was reported, which would otherwise suggest Anorexia Nervosa binge-purge subtype (F50.02). The clinical picture is most consistent with Bulimia Nervosa (F50.2).

confirmed_symptoms: Eating large amounts of food (full takeout meal plus chips and sweets) in a discrete period
Subjective loss of control ('I just keep going')
Shock/distress at the amount eaten afterward
Excessive exercise (long runs) to 'burn off' calories
